glass: copita (small tulip-shaped tasting glass), chilled, no ice
version: v2 (round 5, 2026-09-30): an 'improved' tequila Martini (Codex pp. 86, 88: a small fruit liqueur added to the Martini formula, peach named). Siembra Azul Blanco, recommended (David Suro-Piñera's own blanco, Codex p. 164; not the bottle on the 2016 bat-friendly list, which is Valles Ancestral: 50%, pit-cooked, smoky, $120-150, Hester F22-F23, C11), with blanc vermouth (Codex p. 73: Dolin blanc in tequila Martini variations) and one teaspoon (5 ml) of crème de pêche (Codex p. 88 Watercress: blanc vermouth with 1/2 tsp crème de pêche, stirred; p. 174 Massenez 'useful in… stirred cocktails'). No agave syrup, no peel, no garnish. Replaces v1's elderflower: a picked flower is exactly what this person doesn't take (whoYouAre: 'You don't pick the flower'). Swept: tequila 38-55%, peach 15-20% and 25-40 g, blanc 10-16 g. v2 note (round 7): the blanc vermouth is French style (Codex p. 72: 'delicate, sweet, and herbal'); values are Dolin blanc's (LI pp. 136-137). Siembra Azul 40% sourced (Hester F25).
